questions.problem:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
5\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+10y=7\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

Find the general solution to this equation given that the complementary solution is ${y}_{c}(x)=A{e}^{-2x},$ where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

$y(x)=A{e}^{-2x}\,+\,($
{{field-1}}
$)\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,+\,($
{{field-2}}
$)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the general solution of an inhomogeneous first-order linear equation with constant coefficients on the left-hand side, we must find the sum of the complementary and particular solutions.

To find the complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ we solve the corresponding homogeneous equation, given by

$$
5\frac{\text{d}{y}_{c}}{\text{d}x}+10{y}_{c}=0.
$$

Solving this equation, we find that the complementary solution is

$$
{y}_{c}=A{e}^{-2x}
$$

where $A$ is an arbitrary constant.

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $7\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first derivative of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=-3\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
5(-3\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+3\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))+10(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))=7\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
(10\alpha +15\beta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+(-15\alpha +10\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)=7\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}10\alpha +15\beta =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)) \\ -15\alpha +10\beta =7\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x))\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{21}{65},\beta =\frac{14}{65}.$

Therefore, 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{21}{65}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+\frac{14}{65}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=A{e}^{-2x}+(-\frac{21}{65})\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+(\frac{14}{65})\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).
$$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is $-3\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ So, we assume the particular solution to be 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants to be determined.

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute ${y}_{p}$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation:

$$
(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡x)-2(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡x)=-3\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

$$
(\beta -2\alpha )\operatorname{cos}⁡x+(-\alpha -2\beta )\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-3\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}\beta -2\alpha =0\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ -\alpha -2\beta =-3\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =\frac{3}{5},$ $\beta =\frac{6}{5}.$

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\frac{6}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).

$$
